summary: 60-foot Aermotor fire tower erected in 1924 in Luther Forest; dismantled and rebuilt at Camp Saratoga in Wilton in 2010; open on set weekends April to October.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor tower with a 7 by 7 ft metal cab; model disputed (LS-40 per the Town, the FFLA grant report and Starr; LS-20 per the NHLR)

access.note: Open on set days: the third weekend of each month, April to October, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m., plus October 2 and 3 in foliage season (Town of Wilton). The 2011 Saratogian report said that, for insurance reasons, visitors would have to be accompanied by a volunteer guide; no newer rule was found.

visit.trail_note: At Camp Saratoga, 93 Scout Road, Wilton, NY 12831, inside Wilton Wildlife Preserve & Park.

facts.agency: Wilton Wildlife Preserve & Park, in cooperation with the Town of Wilton

events.note: Erected by the New York Conservation Commission as a 60-foot Aermotor on Cornell Hill in Luther Forest
First forest fire observer Noah LaCasse, 1924 to 1935
State operation ended with the 1970 fire season; the tower was then decommissioned
Saratogian: William Mackay bought the tower from the state for $1 through a surplus program. Starr instead says it was sold to Luther Forest for a nominal fee after decommissioning.
Date registered on the National Historic Lookout Register
Dismantled at Cornell Hill from August 2010; rebuilt at Camp Saratoga by early December 2010
Restored and re-erected by Dave Vana's crew before the move was complete
Dedication ceremony on May 14, 2011; first public access announced for June 4 and 5
FFLA restoration grant of $500 toward furnishing the cab with a map table and fire finder equipment
NHLR visit report (September 16, 2017): excellent condition, wheelchair accessible to the base, volunteers staff the second weekend of each month

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR page says the tower is an LS-20. The Town of Wilton, the FFLA 2011 grant report and Starr all say LS-40. The story reports the LS-40 view as the majority and notes the NHLR difference.

The brief said 2008. The NHLR text says 2011, but its photo caption says re-erected December 2010. Starr and the Saratogian put dismantling in August 2010 and reconstruction in early December 2010. The story follows the 2010 account.

The Saratogian says William Mackay bought the tower from the state for $1 in 1976 through a surplus program. Starr says it was sold to the Luther Forest for a nominal fee after decommissioning, with no year given. Both are reported in the story and neither is treated as settled.

The 2017 NHLR visit report says volunteers staff the second weekend of each month. The Town of Wilton page says the tower opens the third weekend of each month. The current Town page is used for the schedule.

notes_for_editor: The brief's Starr PDF link (nhlr.org/nhlr.org/media/...) returns 404; the working URL is nhlr.org/media/2967/... and is used here. The brief's 2008 relocation is contradicted by the Starr article and the Saratogian and is corrected to 2010. A web search snippet for Wikipedia's Cornell Hill page says summer 2008; that page was not read and is not cited. The ownership question (Mackay purchase in 1976 versus a nominal-fee sale after decommissioning) is unresolved and should be checked before publication. The current Town of Wilton rules page was not read, so today's guided-visit rule is unknown. The local record ../us-ny-cornell-hill/ was not read. The Starr article is a two-column PDF, so some quotes are split on single column lines; those were chosen to stay inside one column.
